In [[Sixth dimension|six-dimensional]] [[Euclidean geometry]], the '''6-simplex honeycomb''' is a space-filling [[tessellation]] (or [[honeycomb (geometry)|honeycomb]]). The tessellation fills space by [[6-simplex]], [[rectified 6-simplex]], and [[birectified 6-simplex]] facets. These facet types occur in proportions of 1:1:1 respectively in the whole honeycomb.

== A6 lattice ==
This [[vertex arrangement]] is called the A6 lattice or '''6-simplex lattice'''. The 42 vertices of the [[expanded 6-simplex]] vertex figure represent the 42 roots of the <math>{\tilde{A}}_6</math> [[Coxeter group]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www2.research.att.com/~njas/lattices/A6.html |title=The Lattice A6 |access-date=2011-05-11 |archive-date=2012-01-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119021529/http://www2.research.att.com/~njas/lattices/A6.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  It is the 6-dimensional case of a [[simplectic honeycomb]]. Around each vertex figure are 126 facets: 7+7 [[6-simplex]], 21+21 [[rectified 6-simplex]], 35+35 [[birectified 6-simplex]], with the count distribution from the 8th row of [[Pascal's triangle]].

The A{{sup sub|*|6}} lattice (also called A{{sup sub|7|6}}) is the union of seven A<sub>6</sub> lattices, and has the [[vertex arrangement]] of the dual to the [[omnitruncated 6-simplex honeycomb]], and therefore the [[Voronoi cell]] of this lattice is the [[omnitruncated 6-simplex]].

== Projection by folding ==

The ''6-simplex honeycomb'' can be projected into the 3-dimensional [[cubic honeycomb]] by a [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Geometric folding|geometric folding]] operation that maps two pairs of mirrors into each other, sharing the same [[vertex arrangement]]:

{|class=wikitable
|-
!<math>{\tilde{A}}_6</math>
|{{CDD|node_1|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|branch}}
|-
!<math>{\tilde{C}}_3</math>
|{{CDD|node_1|4|node|3|node|4|node}}
|}
